checks.finding: The Architecture section provides a top-level Mermaid interaction diagram and a component inventory covering fixtures, Bash and PowerShell suites, golden artifacts, the run-record schema, and existing workflow consumers; the layer specifications consistently elaborate those boundaries.
The directed relationships in the Architecture diagram and component descriptions form an acyclic fixture-to-suite-to-artifact/schema flow, with no circular dependency introduced.
The Data Plan explicitly includes Data Entities, Existing Data Affected, Migration Strategy, persisted-field schemas, invariants, and additive compatibility behavior.

The API / Contract Plan enumerates the affected public and private function signatures, CLI flags, output contracts, schemas, and all four flag combinations; the migration and constraint sections state that the changes are additive and do not break existing consumers.

The Security Boundaries section identifies trust boundaries, authentication and authorization posture, data classification, OWASP considerations, and mitigations; security-spec.md expands the B1-B5 threat surfaces and verification approach.

No frontend/backend integration surface exists for this test-infrastructure specification: frontend-spec.md declares the UI layer not applicable, while the design is limited to local scripts, fixtures, and JSON evidence contracts.

The Test Strategy defines integration and unit-scope rationale, fixture and stub conventions, acceptance mapping, executable commands, evidence artifacts, and CI registration. The known AC-026 firing-semantics gap is disclosed consistently, and the Round 12 amendment supplies a concrete resolution vehicle requiring the semantics fix, AC-009 hash amendment, and TEST-026 extension on the existing TEST-018/TEST-019 harness in the same change.

Every component and contract referenced by the architecture and API plan is defined in the component inventory, contract tables, layer specifications, or established by the cited investigation evidence.

The ADR Change Log identifies the governing ADRs and explains that the additive test-infrastructure work introduces no new architecture decision; investigation.md supplies repository evidence for the referenced ADR context.
The design explicitly declares ds_profile: none and no user-facing interface is in scope, so design-system conformance is not applicable.
No domain specification directory exists for this repository, so domain-conformance review is not applicable.
